diagnosis_explanation:
Your body has a lot of extra weight. This is called morbid obesity. You had surgery to help with this. It is called a gastric bypass. This surgery helps you eat less food. It also helps your body use food better.

You also have high blood pressure. This is called hypertension. It means the force of blood on your artery walls is too high. Your body also had trouble breathing when you slept. This is called sleep apnea. You use a machine called CPAP. It helps you breathe while you sleep.
medication_rationale:
Omeprazole:
This medicine helps protect your stomach. It reduces the amount of acid your stomach makes. You may notice less heartburn. You might get mild stomach upset. This is normal and should pass. Call your doctor if you get a bad rash or trouble breathing.

Lortab:
This medicine helps relieve pain. It is a strong pain reliever. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. It is important to be careful when moving. You may get constipated. Drink plenty of fluids. Call your doctor if you feel very sleepy or have trouble breathing.

Heparin:
This medicine is a blood thinner. It helps prevent blood clots from forming. You may notice a small bump or bruise where the shot is given. This is normal. Call your doctor if you see any bleeding that will not stop. Also call if you have a bad headache or notice blood in your urine.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore from the surgery.
- You may need help with daily tasks.
- Drink bariatric clear liquids. Aim for 64 ounces each day.
- Do not lift anything heavy or strain yourself.
- Your goal this week is to drink 2 ounces per hour.
- Walk short distances inside your home.
- Call your doctor for any significant concerning complaints.

**Week 2:**
- You should start to feel a little stronger.
- You can drink more bariatric clear liquids. Aim for 64 ounces each day.
- Advance to drinking 4 ounces per hour.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting or straining.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little more.
- Drains were removed, so watch the incision sites.
- Call your doctor for any significant concerning complaints.

**Week 3:**
- You can increase your activity level slowly.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
- Keep drinking bariatric clear liquids. Aim for 64 ounces each day.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting or straining.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 5 minutes.
- Make sure incision sites are healing well.
- Call your doctor for any significant concerning complaints.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel more energy this week.
- You can do more light activities at home.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting or straining.
- Keep up with drinking 64 ounces of bariatric clear liquids daily.
- Your goal this week is to walk longer each day.
- Continue to wear your SCDs as instructed.
- Call your doctor for any significant concerning complaints.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your recovery will take time. Be patient with yourself.
- Continue to follow all activity and diet instructions.
- Progress happens gradually.
- You will feel better each week.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.

Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
